$schema_note: Points where source/circular-34-2010.pdf does not determine an outcome. `required_resolution` is null on every entry by design: resolving these is an institutional decision, not an encoding decision.
method_note: A1 was known before this work began. A2 to A6 were found by reading the source clause by clause and asking, at each, what a case would need that the text does not supply. A1 is not the only one and treating it as the only one understates the position materially: A2 and A3 are each decisive on outcomes, and A2 is arguably more consequential than A1 because it governs the deficient-but-timely case that a dispute process actually generates.

ambiguities.question: Is the fourth-paragraph period of `cuarenta y cinco Días` counted in business days or calendar days?

competing_readings.basis: `Días` is capitalised, and the definitions section defines `Días Hábiles` as a term of art. Capitalisation in this instrument marks defined terms, so a capitalised `Días` may be a shortened reference to the defined term.

The definitions section defines `Días Hábiles`, not `Días`. The fifth paragraph, in the same numeral, says `ciento ochenta días naturales` and `cuarenta y cinco días naturales` in lower case and explicitly natural. A drafter distinguishing the two within one numeral arguably signals that the capitalised bare `Días` is neither.

ambiguities.textual_basis: p.13 fourth paragraph reads `cuarenta y cinco Días`. p.14 fifth paragraph reads `ciento ochenta días naturales` and `cuarenta y cinco días naturales`. The definitions section (p.1) defines `Días Hábiles` and does not define `Días`.
ambiguities.materiality: Decisive. On a 45-unit period the two readings diverge by roughly three weeks, and the seventh paragraph makes firmeza turn on exactly this expiry.

ambiguities.question: Does `en los términos señalados` in the firmeza paragraph refer to the timing terms only, or to the full content specification of the fourth paragraph?

competing_readings.basis: The sentence opens with the elapse of the period, so `los términos señalados` may refer back to the delivery obligation as timed.

`el referido dictamen` refers to the dictamen as specified in the fourth paragraph, which includes the `por lo menos` element floor, the plain-language requirement, the authorised signatory and the channel. On this reading a timely but non-conforming dictamen does not prevent firmeza.

ambiguities.textual_basis: p.14 seventh paragraph: `la Emisora no entrega el referido dictamen en los términos señalados`.
ambiguities.materiality: Decisive for any case where a dictamen was delivered inside the period but is deficient on an element. The two readings give opposite answers on whether the credit becomes final.

ambiguities.question: What standard does `acredite al Tarjetahabiente` set, and to whose satisfaction?

competing_readings.reading: Delivery of the conforming dictamen is itself the demonstration
competing_readings.basis: The fourth paragraph opens `Para efectos del primer párrafo del presente numeral`, tying the dictamen to the first paragraph's demonstration requirement.

competing_readings.reading: The dictamen is necessary but not sufficient
competing_readings.basis: The first paragraph requires demonstrating that the charge derived from a 2.6(a) operation. The dictamen is a document that must contain certain elements; containing them is not the same as establishing the fact, and `por lo menos` explicitly declines to make the element list complete.

ambiguities.textual_basis: p.13 first and fourth paragraphs read together.
ambiguities.materiality: Determines whether the recovery right can ever be established mechanically. Under the second reading it cannot.

ambiguities.question: Which event starts the period where more than one notice was presented, or where a notice was presented to an entity other than the issuer?

competing_readings.basis: The text says `el aviso a que se refiere el numeral 3.3`, definite singular.
3.3 permits two distinct notice types, and a case may involve both a theft notice and a later unrecognised-charge claim over the same charge.

ambiguities.textual_basis: p.13 fourth paragraph `contado a partir de la fecha en la que se haya recibido el aviso a que se refiere el numeral 3.3`; p.10 numeral 3.3 first paragraph enumerating two notice types.
ambiguities.materiality: Changes the deadline by the interval between the two notices. Not addressed by the source.

ambiguities.question: Who determines, and on what evidence, whether the issuer `cuenta con` the device address?

competing_readings.basis: The condition is about the issuer's own holdings, which only the issuer can report.
Reading it as issuer assertion makes inciso d) unfalsifiable: an issuer that omits the field and asserts it holds nothing cannot be contradicted from the record.

ambiguities.textual_basis: p.14 inciso d) `En caso de contar con ella`.
ambiguities.materiality: Determines whether inciso d) is a requirement or a self-certification. Does not change outcomes in cases where the address is supplied.

ambiguities.question: To whom must the dictamen be made available, given that numeral 3.4 names a different recipient for the same document?

competing_readings.basis: 3.6's fourth paragraph says `poner a disposición del Tarjetahabiente`, and 3.4's second paragraph also says `entregue al Tarjetahabiente un dictamen`.
3.4's third paragraph says `La Emisora deberá entregar al Titular el dictamen a que se refiere el párrafo anterior en términos del numeral 3.6`, naming the Titular for a document specified by 3.6.

ambiguities.textual_basis: p.12 numeral 3.4 second and third paragraphs against p.13 numeral 3.6 fourth paragraph. The instrument treats Titular and Tarjetahabiente as distinct roles throughout.
ambiguities.materiality: Determines who can complain that the dictamen was not made available, and therefore who can trigger the firmeza consequence.
